cita: Jiang et al. (2026). KRCA: An Efficient Root Cause Analysis System in Hyper-Scale Microservice Systems via Agentic AI.
notes: Sec.3.4/Fig.6: three-tier memory (Working=per-service short-term dialogue with cross-service activation -> TRABAJO; Factual=service-specific historical failures -> EPISODICA; Experiential=generalized reasoning insights e.g. 'traffic saturation causes MySQL slow queries' -> SEMANTICA), all text/RAG entries -> representacion=DOCS-ARCHIVOS. RAG retrieval top-3 per Eq.6 hybrid score = alpha*BM25(service names)+beta*BM25(metric names)+gamma*exp(-lambda*age) -> retrieval=RANKING (lexical BM25 + temporal weighting, no dense embeddings described). Self-reflection phase 'distills case-specific details and generalizable insights into the memory system... after each resolved alert' -> operaciones=WRITE(Factual case write)+CONSOLIDACION(distillation into Experiential); trigger=EVENTO-DETERMINISTA (alert-resolution checkpoint, not LLM-discretionary). Table2 ablation w/o Tiered Memory: Root-Cause AC@1 0.88->0.81 (Failure-Type AC@1 0.79->0.74); w/ Naive RAG (flat pool, uniform weights) AC@1 0.88->0.78 -> mide_lectura=SI/RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO, evidencia_tipo=ABLATION. Table1: KRCA AC@1=0.88/0.79 vs strongest baseline RCA-Agent 0.57/0.47 (+31%/+32% abs); production deployment reduces avg diagnosis time -77.3% (abstract) -> metricas=EXITO;LATENCIA, evidencia_tipo=BENCHMARK-E2E. F differs from F_screening(MULTIAGENTE): added WRITE (self-reflection memory write), RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO (ablation above), COSTO (latency/production-time reduction is the paper's efficiency claim). No named public benchmark, proprietary 300-case Kuaishou production dataset (Sec.4.1) -> benchmarks=NINGUNO. Main Agent (global RAG query) + 9 domain Sub Agents (task-specific RAG query) share the SAME Factual/Experiential memory pool -> multiagente=SI, handoff=CONTENIDO (evidence tuples/insights shared main<->sub and across future incidents). No staleness/provenance check on stored cases/insights described -> fidelidad_procedencia=NO. alcance=ORGANIZACION: memory accumulates across ALL resolved alerts spanning Kuaishou's whole hyper-scale system (200k+ services, multiple business lines/teams), not bounded to one task/project. plan_estado=NO (no plan/progress-tracking content).

benchmarks: 2WikiMultiHopQA, MuSiQue, GAIA, FRAMES, DeepResearch Bench, SWE-bench-Verified
fallos_mitigaciones: App.F case studies: SOP over-generalization (stored SOP lacked exclusion criteria, misclassified a high-risk symptom cluster as routine) and Retrieval/Recall errors (incomplete patient-specific memory combined with general knowledge produced an overconfident wrong answer); paper RECOMMENDS (not yet implemented) provenance/timestamps/confidence fields + mandatory applicability checks before SOP execution.
cita: Zhang et al. (2026). StackPlanner: A Centralized Hierarchical Multi-Agent System with Task-Experience Memory Management.
notes: Fig.1/Sec.3.1-3.3: task memory stack M (short-term execution trace of coordinator, per-task) -> TRABAJO; 'semantic memory, which stores factual knowledge and declarative information' -> SEMANTICA; 'procedural memory (SOPs), which abstracts key execution steps from previously completed tasks' -> PROCEDIMENTAL (a user-profile component is also stored but has no clean vocab match, not counted separately). App.H: SOP/semantic memory stored in a Faiss vector DB with top-k vector retrieval (<800ms avg latency); task stack is plain pushed/popped text -> representacion=HIBRIDA, retrieval=EMBEDDINGS. Sec.3.1 REVISE={Update(push,WRITE), Condensation(pop+summarize+push,CONSOLIDACION), Pruning(remove segment,OLVIDO)} -> operaciones=WRITE;CONSOLIDACION;OLVIDO; trigger=DISCRECIONAL-LLM (RL-trained coordinator policy decides WHEN to REVISE -- the paper's central contribution vs passive/fixed strategies). Table4 ablation (Qwen2.5-3B): Ours 2Wiki/MuSiQue/GAIA/FRAMES=32.92/16.48/7.71/16.23 vs w/o-Task-Memory 29.90/10.76/4.68/13.53 vs w/o-Experience 28.47/8.99/5.53/7.69 vs w/o-Both 17.12/7.43/2.47/6.33 -> mide_lectura=SI/RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO, evidencia_tipo=ABLATION. Table1 SOTA vs OWL/MacNet/AFlow/ReSearch/ARPO -> evidencia_tipo=BENCHMARK-E2E. Table11(App.G): StackPlanner vs ReAct=880.89 vs 1597.09 avg tokens, 10.15s vs 30.49s avg time, 11.38 vs 14.51 avg iterations -> metricas=EXITO;ITERACION;COSTO-TOKENS;LATENCIA, evidencia_tipo also MEDICION-COSTO. F differs from F_screening(MULTIAGENTE;RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO): added WRITE, CONSOLIDACION (REVISE sub-ops above), COSTO (Table11), NEGATIVO (App.F qualitative failure cases show memory-induced wrong answers -> evidencia negativa sobre memoria; also adds evidencia_tipo=CUALITATIVA). App.F explicitly recommends but does NOT implement provenance/timestamp/confidence fields after observing failures -> fidelidad_procedencia=NO. Central-Sub Interface passes 'Subtask Requirements'(spec sub-agent must follow=CONTRATO)+'Subtask Result'(=CONTENIDO) -> handoff=CONTENIDO;CONTRATO. Task memory records task specs/coordinator messages/sub-agent I-O consulted by the PLAN action = live progress log -> plan_estado=SI. Sec.'Human-in-the-Loop'/Table3: multi-turn refinement reopens loop from preserved task state, user profile keyed by user identifier (App.H) -> alcance=SESION. Search/Report/Human sub-agents + coordinator query the SAME experience memory ('Have I answered a similar question before?') -> multiagente=SI.

fallos_mitigaciones: Sec.1/2: preprocessing paradigms cause 'destructive de-contextualization' and LLMs fall into 'Lost-in-the-Middle' when raw chunks are concatenated (Table6, Direct-Read collapse); mitigated by isolating each episodic context in a dedicated Assistant agent (parallel local reasoning, no cross-chunk concatenation) plus explicit temporal-anchoring conflict resolution (Eq.9) at aggregation time.
cita: Wang et al. (2026). E-mem: Multi-Agent Based Episodic Context Reconstruction for LLM Agent Memory.
notes: Sec.3.2/3.3: sliding-window episodic contexts Ei preserved verbatim per assistant agent (no compression) -> mem_tipos=EPISODICA. Si=<Ei,si> dual-representation: raw token sequence (DOCS-ARCHIVOS) + dense/sparse routing signals (Pglobal/Pvec = vector similarity over summaries/raw chunks -> VECTOR; Pkw = BM25 symbolic-entity match -> GREP-ARCHIVOS) -> representacion=HIBRIDA, retrieval=EMBEDDINGS;GREP-ARCHIVOS. 'Incremental Updates': O(1) streaming appends to active context; 'When capacity L is reached, the context is solidified as a completed memory unit' -> operaciones=WRITE;ACTUALIZACION, trigger=PRESUPUESTO (token-capacity threshold, not an LLM judgment or external event). Table6 ablation MAS vs 'Simpler Pipeline (Direct-Read, single LLM over concatenated raw chunks)': Overall F1 54.17 vs 38.27 (LoCoMo); Fig.3b router-pathway ablation: full 55.76 -> w/o Pglobal 45.30(-10.46) -> w/o Pvec 47.90 -> w/o Pkw 52.42 -> mide_lectura=SI/RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO, evidencia_tipo=ABLATION. Table1/2: E-mem beats GAM by +8.86%F1(GPT-4o-mini)/+6.63%(Qwen2.5-14B) on LoCoMo, +6.51%F1 vs RAG on HotpotQA-1600 -> evidencia_tipo=BENCHMARK-E2E, benchmarks=LoCoMo, HotpotQA. Table7/Sec.4.5 Normalized-Cost (Large-vs-Small-model token split, 1:10 ratio) shows E-mem reduces token cost >70% vs baselines at comparable/better F1 -> metricas=EXITO;COSTO-TOKENS, evidencia_tipo also MEDICION-COSTO. Eq.9: master agent 'compares absolute timestamps tau...prioritizing the most recent information to construct a cohesive...logical chain' when evidence conflicts across memory units -> fidelidad_procedencia=SI/FIDELIDAD. F differs from F_screening(MULTIAGENTE;RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO): added WRITE, COSTO, FIDELIDAD (all above). Global routing summaries si act as lightweight pointers into the archived raw context, while evidence tuples ei=<ci,tau_i> are the content surfaced to the master -> handoff=PUNTEROS;CONTENIDO. LoCoMo is explicitly a 'multi-session dialogues' benchmark (Sec.4.1) -> alcance=SESION. Master+multiple Assistant agents jointly reason over a SHARED episodic archive (Fig.2) -> multiagente=SI. No plan/progress-state content described (memory=conversational facts/events, not task plans) -> plan_estado=NO.

benchmarks: UltraChat, UltraFeedback, Prm800k, Gsm8k, APIGen, AgentGym
fallos_mitigaciones: Streaming insertions interleaved with search cause 'frequent staleness of the cached clusters' (Sec.'CPU-GPU coordinated index management'); mitigated by an insertion buffer + asynchronous CPU-GPU transfer, and by agent-workload-aware multi-level caching that re-promotes hot clusters.
cita: Hu et al. (2026). Pancake: Hierarchical Memory System for Multi-Agent LLM Serving.
notes: System/infra paper: Pancake is a serving-layer ANN-index optimizer sitting BENEATH arbitrary agent memory content (integrates into Mem-GPT/LangChain/LlamaIndex, Sec.1/Fig.1) -- it does not itself define a memory TYPE, mem_tipos=NA (measures/accelerates retrieval latency+recall of whatever memory an integrated agent stores, per rule 5). Sec.2.1/Fig.3: memory items are embedding vectors indexed via IVF/HNSW/Vamana-style clusters -> representacion=VECTOR; Sec.'hybrid graph' connects multiple agents' coarse indexes for unified upper-level search -> retrieval=EMBEDDINGS;GRAFO. Fig.2 code example: mm.Insert/mm.Update/mm.Delete calls issued directly by CALLING agents (Pancake doesn't decide WHEN to write, only serves the op) -> operaciones=WRITE;ACTUALIZACION;OLVIDO, trigger=NA (write-timing decision is external/out of scope for this infra paper). Fig.16 'Tradeoff between recall and query latency': Pancake vs plain IVF baseline at fixed recall targets (IVF must scan up to 128 clusters for high recall, degrades further under mixed search-update workload) -> mide_lectura=SI/RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO, evidencia_tipo=ABLATION (also Sec.6.1 Pancake-IVF-Static/Pancake-IVF-Split maintenance-strategy variants). Fig.12-15: end-to-end throughput vs Mem-GPT/LangMem/LlamaIndex baselines, >4.29x average speedup, memory-op time share cut to ~3.2% (from up to 82-99%, Fig.1/Sec.2.2) -> evidencia_tipo=BENCHMARK-E2E;MEDICION-COSTO, metricas=LATENCIA(throughput/query latency)+OTRA(recall). Datasets: UltraChat, UltraFeedback, Prm800k, Gsm8k, APIGen, AgentGym (Sec.6.1) -- no single named 'memory' benchmark. Fig.2 explicit multi-agent example: Agent1 writes D(index1,shared); Agent2 searches[1,2,3], plans P, inserts P(index3); Agent3 codes C from M2, updates index2; Agent4 validates, deletes P, inserts improved R -> handoff=CONTENIDO (D/P/C/R pass between agents via shared/partially-shared indexes), plan_estado=SI (a 'Plan' P is explicitly written/read/later superseded as memory content), multiagente=SI ('fully/partially shared' memory scopes across agents, Fig.2). alcance=PROYECTO: the deployed memory system serves one multi-agent application's full workload (Task Planning/Knowledge/Code/Action-History/Research/User-profile, 1K-8M items), not scoped to one task/session nor explicitly multi-tenant-org. No provenance/staleness-of-CONTENT verification (only system-level cache consistency) -> fidelidad_procedencia=NO. F differs from F_screening(RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO;MULTIAGENTE): added COSTO (extensive latency/throughput measurement, core contribution) and WRITE (insert/update/delete interleaving is the paper's central technical problem).

fallos_mitigaciones: Risk of bad/incorrect entries polluting institutional memory; mitigated by 4-node BFT weighted-consensus validation before any commit (e.g. red-team report accepted at score=0.88) + RBAC clearance levels limiting write/read scope by department (Sec.2.1/4.4). Sec.4.2 also flags an epistemic-attribution caveat (cannot cleanly separate 'emergent expertise' from LLM training-data recombination), acknowledged but not a memory-staleness/poisoning issue per se.
cita: Kannabhiran (2026). Institutional Memory as Organizational Knowledge: AI Agents That Learn Their Jobs from Experience, Not Instructions.
notes: Sec.2.3/2.5/4.4: 8 seed entries (handbook, scoring rubric, difficulty definitions, pipeline workflow, dept. responsibilities, calibration baselines, hardening techniques, generation patterns) = declarative/organizational facts -> SEMANTICA; hardening-techniques/pipeline-workflow/generation-patterns = reusable SOPs -> PROCEDIMENTAL; CEO 'queries (S)AGE for historical performance before each pipeline run' + Sec.4.4 committed pentest report becomes queryable precedent for FUTURE runs -> EPISODICA. Sec.2.3 'Agents...query this knowledge via domain-tagged similarity search' -> representacion=HIBRIDA (structured text entries + similarity-search index), retrieval=EMBEDDINGS. Sec.2.3/4.4: entries 'submitted...validated through weighted consensus, and committed' (4-node BFT) -> operaciones=WRITE;ADMISION (consensus IS the admission gate); write happens when CEO 'summarizes and submits pipeline observations AFTER EACH RUN' -> trigger=EVENTO-DETERMINISTA (post-run checkpoint). Sec.3 Identity-Verification test: 11/11 agents correctly answer 6 org-context questions using ONLY seed knowledge, none of which is in their 3-line prompts -> mide_lectura=SI/RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO (measures whether retrieved institutional knowledge is correctly used). Sec.6 'Scope clarification: the present paper is a systems demonstration, NOT a statistical performance study'; the Treatment-vs-Control SAGE-enabled/disabled ablation (Experiment B, Sec.6.1) is explicitly PROPOSED FUTURE WORK, not run here -> evidencia_tipo=CUALITATIVA (single end-to-end pipeline run, Table2/Table4) + MEDICION-COSTO (quantified: 508s pipeline, 525.2s blind solve, 16384 queries, Table2-4) -- NOT ABLATION. metricas=EXITO(quality 93.0/100, calibration gap 0.20);ITERACION(2 hardening iters, 3 solver iters);LATENCIA(per-stage times, Table2/4). Sec.5.2/Table1: (S)AGE RBAC enforces department-scoped clearance (1=own-dept,2=cross-dept,3=admin) ON-CHAIN over the SAME institutional KB read/written by all 11 agents+CEO -> multiagente=SI; consensus-gated commit (score=0.88 threshold)+RBAC = security-of-memory (poisoning/unauthorized-write resistance) -> fidelidad_procedencia=SI/FIDELIDAD, F adds SEGURIDAD. Sec.4.4: pentest report (CONTENIDO) is committed and 'available to all future agents'; scoring rubric/difficulty-definitions function as a shared CONTRATO all agents must satisfy -> handoff=CONTENIDO;CONTRATO. alcance=ORGANIZACION (explicit whole-company: 5 depts/11 agents/RBAC clearance spanning the org). No public benchmark, proprietary CTF demo -> benchmarks=NINGUNO. F differs from F_screening(WRITE;MULTIAGENTE;FIDELIDAD): added RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO, SEGURIDAD, PROCEDIMENTAL (all justified above). plan_estado=NO (pipeline routing-state lives in separate deterministic code, not queried as (S)AGE memory content).

fallos_mitigaciones: Eq.8 retrieval reward beta=0.2 explicitly weighted 'to prioritize retrieval precision while minimizing noise for answer generation' -- a design mitigation against over-retention/noisy-retrieval degrading downstream accuracy (Sec.4.1, Fig.3 sensitivity study).
cita: Mao et al. (2026). Joint Optimization of Multi-agent Memory System.
notes: Sec.4.1: Extraction Agent builds fine-grained memory Mf ('key events and facts') -> EPISODICA; Profile Agent abstracts coarse-grained Mc ('users' stable preferences/behavioral patterns') from Mf -> SEMANTICA. App.B.3 prompts: both stored/passed as plain text in the agent prompts (fine-grained + coarse-grained memory blocks), no vector-DB described for CoMAM's OWN store (only the RAG baseline uses embeddings, App.B.2) -> representacion=DOCS-ARCHIVOS. Retrieval Agent prompt (App.B.3, 'Retrieve relevant memory to answer the following question...output retrieved info in <information>') reads the full Mf+Mc as text and selects/ranks relevant content -> retrieval=RANKING (LLM-driven selection, no ANN backend for CoMAM itself). Eq.6-7: Extraction reward=evidence-coverage, Profile reward=LLM-judged abstraction quality of Mc relative to H -> operaciones=WRITE(extraction)+CONSOLIDACION(profile abstraction from fine memory); deterministic per-query pipeline (not gated by an external event/budget check) -> trigger=EVENTO-DETERMINISTA. Table3(RQ2) ablation on PersonaMem: Ours 0.64/0.70/0.66(32K/128K/1M) vs Base(no agents) 0.23/0.26/0.37, w/o-Ex 0.52/0.52/0.51, w/o-Pr 0.57/0.52/0.57, w/o-Re 0.54/0.51/0.51, w/o-train variants -2..-8%; Table4(RQ3) single-vs-heterogeneous-policy x independent-vs-end-to-end-RL; Table5/Fig.4(RQ4) local-only/global-only/uniform-LG vs adaptive-credit-assignment -> mide_lectura=SI/RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO (Re-agent explicitly ablated), evidencia_tipo=ABLATION. Table1: PersonaMem QA accuracy across 32K/128K/1M x Qwen/Llama, CoMAM 0.64-0.70 vs best baseline Memory-R1 0.57-0.61 (+8.5% to +16.7%); Table2 LongMemEval best-across-all-metrics vs GAM -> evidencia_tipo=BENCHMARK-E2E, benchmarks=PersonaMem, LongMemEval. Table6 reports RL convergence steps -> metricas=EXITO;ITERACION. Extraction/Profile/Retrieval agents are jointly trained (MDP, Sec.4.2) and consume/produce the SAME memory set M={Mf,Mc} -> multiagente=SI (matches F_screening). Memory M persists past construction to answer SUBSEQUENT queries within the same multi-session conversational history (PersonaMem/LongMemEval = multi-session benchmarks) -> alcance=SESION, handoff=CONTENIDO. No provenance/staleness verification of stored memory content described -> fidelidad_procedencia=NO; no plan/progress-tracking content (memory=facts/preferences, not task state) -> plan_estado=NO. F differs from F_screening(MULTIAGENTE only): added RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO, WRITE, CONSOLIDACION (all justified above). NOTE: PDF header title reads 'Joint Optimization of Multi-agent Memory System' (input metadata title differs slightly, 'Collaborative Multi-Agent Optimization for Personalized Memory System') but abstract/method (CoMAM, MDP formulation, NDCG-based adaptive credit assignment, local+global rewards) match the input abstract exactly -- same paper, citation uses the PDF's own title.
